title: Word Wizard
brief: Your Word Wizard takes any word and transforms it three ways: it measures the length, grabs the first few letters with a slice, and swaps letters with .replace(). The length spell is written for you as an example.

problem.goal: Print the length of the word, its first three letters, and the word with every "a" swapped for an "o".
rules: The length must come from len(), not from counting the letters yourself.
The first three letters come from a slice, so it works for any word.
Every "a" is swapped, not only the first one.
A word with no "a" in it is fine: it simply comes out unchanged.

steps: The program asks for a word and stores it in the variable word.
The length spell is done for you as an example: print("Length:", len(word)).
Print the first three letters using a slice.
Print the word with every "a" replaced by an "o", using .replace().
Run it, type a word, then press Check project.
starterCode:
# 🪄 Word Wizard: it transforms any word you give it!

word = input("Give me a word: ")

# The length spell is done for you as an example:
print("Length:", len(word))

# 1) Print just the first THREE letters, using a slice:


# 2) Print the word with every "a" replaced by an "o", using .replace():
hints: Run it first. The length line already works, which shows you the shape the other two lines should take: a label, a comma, then the value.
A slice of the first three letters is word[:3]. You could also write word[0:3], since leaving the start out means the same as starting at 0.
Do not slice with word[3], which is a single letter at index 3, not the first three. The colon is what makes it a slice.
.replace takes two pieces of text: what to find and what to put there. So word.replace("a", "o") reads as replace every a with an o.
Remember that neither the slice nor the replace changes word itself. Both hand back a new string, which is fine here because you print it straight away.
inputHint: Type one word for the wizard to transform.
successMessage: Magical! You measured, sliced and transformed text like a true Word Wizard. len(), slicing and .replace() are the three string tools you will reach for most often.
